protocol: docs/Korean IGT – Experimental Plan & Baselines.pdf (v1.1), sections 6.1-6.5 and 7.2 (agenda 17 Nov: 1B only)

adapter.target_modules_note: Bolmo-1B = byte-level local encoder/decoder (xLSTM) around a 16-layer global transformer. LoRA goes on q_proj/v_proj of the 16 global layers only (32 modules); the regex excludes the boundary predictor's q_proj_layer and the xLSTM q/k/v. The runner fails if the match count is 0 and records the matched names.

training.max_seq_bytes_note: Bolmo is byte-level. Longest train example is 1470 bytes (3 of 2079 exceed 1024), dev/test max 896, so 1536 keeps every example untruncated.
training.precision: bf16 on GPUs with compute capability >= 8 (A100, L4), else float32 (T4)
training.eval_every_epochs_note: The plan saves after each epoch; every 0.5 epoch is a superset (epochs 1, 2, 3 are among the six checkpoints) and is kept for all runs so they stay comparable.
training.resume_every_steps_note: Quick resume save (adapter + optimizer state, overwritten each time, not evaluated) so a Colab disconnect loses at most 20 optimizer steps.
training.two_stage_teacher_forcing: stage-2 training and validation-loss examples use the gold transliteration; validation/test generation always chains the predicted transliteration

runs_note: Plan section 6.2: A baseline (r16, alpha 32, lr 2e-4), B lr1e-4, C r8 (alpha 16), D r32 (alpha 64). A and B have priority; C and D are optional extensions if compute allows. The plan's LoRA setup is the two-stage pipeline, so B-D run on two_stage; all_in_one LoRA is an extra baseline.

generation.max_new_bytes_note: Longest gold answer: train gloss 265 bytes, dev/test gloss 116 bytes. Training appends an end-of-sequence byte, so the model learns to stop.
